hints: Look at how the halogens change as you go down Group 17, think colour, state and strength in one smooth trend.
Iodine is already a black solid and a fairly weak oxidiser, so ask yourself what comes next for astatine below it.
Remember that H-X bond strength gets weaker down the group, so decide which of the three statements can survive that trend.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 17 trends down the group**

Think of fluorine at the top to iodine lower down. Colour gets darker, state gets more solid, oxidising power gets weaker, and hydride stability gets lower.

Trend down: $\text{F}_2 > \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2 > \text{At}_2$ for oxidising strength

**Check statement 1, colour and state**

Chlorine is a pale green gas, bromine is a brown liquid, iodine is a shiny black solid. Continuing the trend, astatine must be even darker and solid.

So: $\text{I}_2\text{(black solid)} \rightarrow \text{At}_2\text{(dark solid)}$ therefore statement 1 is true.

**Check statement 2, oxidising power**

Oxidising power depends on gaining an electron. Atoms get bigger down the group, so the nucleus attracts a new electron less strongly.

$$\text{Oxidising power: } \text{F}_2 > \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2 > \text{At}_2$$
So astatine is a weaker oxidiser than iodine, statement 2 is false.

**Check statement 3, hydride stability**

Thermal stability of $\text{HX}$ depends on H-X bond strength. Larger halogen atoms make longer, weaker bonds.

$$\text{Stability: } \text{HF} > \text{HCl} > \text{HBr} > \text{HI} > \text{HAt}$$
$\text{HI}$ already decomposes easily on heating, so $\text{HAt}$ will be even less stable. Statement 3 is false.

**Combine to choose**

Only statement 1 is true. That corresponds to 1 only.

options.A: This would mean all three statements are true. Statements 2 and 3 go against the Group 17 trends, astatine is weaker as an oxidiser and its hydride is weaker, so this cannot be correct.
options.B: This would mean 1 and 2 are true. Statement 1 is true, but statement 2 reverses the trend. Oxidising power decreases down the group, so At is less powerful than iodine, not more.
options.C: This would mean 2 and 3 are true. Both are false. Students sometimes think bigger atoms gain electrons more easily or make stronger bonds, but in Group 17 the opposite is true down the group.
options.D: This means only 1 is correct. Astatine continues the trend from iodine to be a dark-coloured solid, while it is a weaker oxidising agent than iodine and forms an unstable hydride HAt.
